claims.statement: SesamParser and the sesam.py __main__ dispatcher own parsing and command admission, while SesamCmdClient owns orchestration, archive/whitelist state, expected-output comparison and scheduler coordination; its SesamNode starts as None and is assigned during online bootstrap.

The CLI parses positional command tokens with nargs='*', lowercases only the first to select one command, and treats the remaining tokens as arguments rather than an ordered multi-command pipeline; format and run-pytest use the first remaining argument and add-datatype uses all remaining arguments as names.
The implemented connector scaffolding command is connector-init, although help spells it connector_init; add-datatype is admitted and dispatched but absent from the help command list.

Validate and format are the exact offline dispatch set, skipping credential resolution, SesamNode construction and the developer-mode check; every other recognized command, including expand, dump, convert, init, connector-init, add-datatype and run-pytest, performs online bootstrap before its handler.

SesamNode decodes the supplied JWT payload to select the first subscription principal, attempts portal analytics before creating sesamclient.Connection, and delegates the external connection and its underlying behavior to the pinned sesamclient dependency.

Portal user-interaction registration posts a subscription ID and api_call action to https://portal.sesam.io/api/analytics with the node JWT as bearer token, skips without a subscription ID, limits attempts to one per 60 seconds per object, has no explicit local POST timeout and debug-logs RequestException instead of propagating it.

Online dispatch requires truthy API status developer_mode, with a -force override limited to upload and download; upload also forwards force to configuration upload, and the override does not unlock other commands on non-developer subscriptions.

Validate is connector-specific and mutating despite being offline: dispatch first regenerates expansion, then checks the manifest's datatype templates and literal .expanded for JSON, warning descriptions and collect/share conventions; template sink.dataset is rejected, invalid results exit 1 and successful validation is logged at WARNING.

Connector expansion reads launch-directory manifest/templates, renders systems, datatype pipes and shim pipes, removes/recreates the requested expanded directory, writes node metadata and copies or creates the selected profile; pipes using a differently named reusable template receive an ignored-during-collapse warning comment.

Expansion can overwrite webhook event-pipe permissions with anonymous write_data access when the manifest uses a webhook secret; collapse removes permissions from matching event pipe components and ignores datatype templates whose basename differs from the datatype.

Connector upload changes into connector_dir, expands, validates, uploads from expanded_dir and authenticates unless -skip-auth; test calls the upload method directly and does not use this connector dispatch wrapper.

The -d, -e and system-placeholder options are branch-specific: direct expand/validate dispatch does not change into -d, validate compares its list-valued args.command to the string 'validate' and scans hard-coded .expanded rather than -e, while update-schemas dispatch changes into -d without forwarding the custom placeholder to its helper.

Local configuration archives contain .conf.json files under pipes and systems plus optional node-metadata.conf.json, exclude expected/testdata, replace any existing sesam-config.zip and remove the temporary archive unless retention is requested; dump retains this local archive.

For regular configuration, online bootstrap optionally parses and logs .jinja_vars; local archiving substitutes its values and download can reverse-substitute them in pipe/system files, while connector configuration does not use this substitution path.

Upload requires the selected profile file, optionally deletes all remote sink datasets, merges parent .additional_parameters.json over profile values, replaces remote environment before uploading configuration, waits for user pipes to deploy and then posts test data; later failures do not roll back earlier remote writes.

Upload rewrites the archive's existing node-metadata entry to disable user scheduling by default and eager microservices by default, with enable-user-pipes, enable-eager-ms and disable-cpp-extensions altering that entry; an omitted entry is not synthesized, and setting these flags on run does not reconfigure the node.

Testdata upload walks JSON files recursively and derives pipe IDs from filenames, uses 8 workers by default, switches to sequential processing with -single-thread-upload, and ignores custom worker counts in that sequential mode; --upload-workers below 1 and negative --upload-rate are parser errors.

Testdata request attempts share a lock-protected rate limiter with default 0 meaning unlimited, including retries; each upload permits four attempts with exponential delay plus jitter for retryable request failures including 429 and server errors, while other ordinary 4xx errors are not retried.

Parallel testdata upload collects failures into TestDataUploadException after processing futures, whereas sequential failure propagates immediately; both paths log progress/summary, and the parallel success message about waiting five seconds has no matching sleep at that point.

Download overwrites the selected profile, normalizes remote configuration and restores/removes temporary metadata settings, deletes selected old local pipe/system files then extracts the full remote ZIP; connector download changes into the expansion directory and subsequently collapses to rewritten templates and manifest.

Status compares local archive/profile against remote configuration/environment using Python unified_diff with optional diff output and archive dump; differences and a missing local profile are logged without raising, and missing connector expansion in dispatch is also a log-only branch.

Connector-init requires a directory name ending -connector and, when manifest is absent, writes an auth-dependent manifest/system template and README and copies a source LICENSE; an existing manifest skips initialization.

Add-datatype requires positional datatype names, overwrites their manifest entries and templates and updates system operations; --share adds share pipes and REST operations, while parsed --datatype is not its datatype selector.

Update-schemas attempts to enable inference metadata, waits for deployment, runs manifest datatype collect pumps, reads entity-types/sink through the external API, writes manual and merged JSON schemas and schema.csv, and warns/skips empty schemas.

Init rewrites local input pipes into conditional prod/test alternatives selected by $ENV(node-env), excludes dataset/merge/union/diff/embedded source types and adds missing test alternatives; optional -add-test-entities fetches at most ten live entities and -force-add permits overwriting existing samples.

Convert operates on conditional embedded source alternatives for the selected profile, changes those alternatives to http_endpoint and writes entities to testdata/<pipe _id>.json; optional -dump archives before conversion and plain embedded sources are not generally converted by this handler.

Format uses the first positional selector with default all, supports pipes/systems/testdata/expected or an explicit .json path, rewrites nonrecursive grouped matches, skips .test.json only in grouped expected formatting, applies expected encoding/HTML-escape policy, and returns normally for invalid non-JSON selectors.

Node URL/JWT resolution is delegated to sesamclient.utils.get_node_and_jwt_token with -node, -jwt and -sync-config-file, defaulting the filename to .syncconfig; internal environment/file precedence and URL normalization are not implemented in this wrapper.

Profile defaults to test and selects upload/download environment filenames, connector expansion profile propagation and conversion alternatives, rather than providing a global filter over all node operations.

Although help documents -single and -sesamconfig-file, neither has an inspected consumer in the CLI/connector modules; current formatting calls use format_json's default style rather than establishing the documented .sesamconfig.json formatting override.

Whitelist loading derives filename, pipe and system lists once; local archive generation filters pipe/system paths and separately conditions metadata inclusion, but upload environment replacement and all-sink-dataset deletion are not whitelist-limited.

Testdata, expected-spec loading, update and verify filter by pipe only when the derived whitelist pipe list is truthy, so a whitelist without pipe entries does not select zero pipes; download's whitelist limits old-file deletion but not whole-ZIP extraction.

Whitelisting is not a global safety boundary: the derived system whitelist has no inspected consumer, and run/stop/authentication/connector expansion and validation/local preparation/format/schema generation/destructive administration do not implement handler-wide whitelist filtering.

Run always stops the prior internal scheduler before starting execution; local node wrappers construct POST run-all-pipes and stop-run-all-pipes plus GET scheduler-log and pipe-runner-status routes under the node API, delegating actual scheduling and stabilization to the backend.

Scheduler controls default to two zero runs, 100 max runs, 900 seconds max time and sync requests; mode and request-mode are locally validated, input-dataset deletion is requested unless local testdata exists, and pipe reset/sink-dataset deletion is requested unless explicitly disabled.

The scheduler worker interprets a sync response or requires an async token and polls status every ten seconds with interaction registration; the foreground completion/log loop sleeps one second, and failed or not-running results lead to RuntimeError.

Scheduler poll frequency is parsed but unused, deprecated scheduler-selection/removal flags do not select another implementation or restore cleanup, and scheduler-node does not redirect the inspected scheduler execution path.

The dispatch finally block only reports elapsed time and performs no automatic scheduler cleanup; timing begins after bootstrap, explicit stop is used before run and wipe, and reset/restart attempt stop with throw_error=False so a stop failure can be logged while administration continues.

Wipe stops scheduling, uploads metadata disabling user scheduling/signalling/C++ extensions followed by an empty configuration, both with API force=True, clears environment and waits for user pipes to disappear; the local code does not independently establish help's user-dataset deletion guarantee.

Reset delegates to reset_node, which help describes as entire database deletion and restart, checks an OK response and polls for changed node_start_time using restart_timeout; it remains developer-gated without a -force override.
Restart delegates to restart_node rather than wipe, requires an OK response and polls for changed node_start_time with restart_timeout after a best-effort scheduler stop.

TestSpec binds expected/*.test.json to pipe/file/endpoint/stage and policy: defaults infer the pipe and .json expected filename from the spec name, use endpoint json and ignore_deletes=True, and sort by _id with serialized-entity tie-breaking; specs may override ignore, blacklist, parameters and sorting fields.

JSON/Excel expected-output testing compares normalized entities: current entities are recursively filtered by blacklist and underscore-key policy retaining _id and true _deleted, unexpected deletes can be ignored, integral floats/Decimals are normalized and legacy large-integer rounding is reproduced unless -no-large-int-bugs is set; XML uses normalized serialization with fallback and other endpoints compare bytes.

Expected-spec loading treats absent pipes/files as verify failures, while update can remove obsolete non-ignored specs, create missing output files/default specs and remove ignored output files; update accepts current live output as a rewritten baseline without running pipes first.

Verify reads live output/endpoint pipes without upload/run, raises for mismatches or missing coverage when specifications exist, but returns with a warning when no test specifications are found; invalid-config pipes are logged and excluded before spec loading.
Published-data retrieval is not purely read-only: SesamNode.get_published_data enables a disabled pump before its GET, affecting publisher-based expected-output update and verification.
Test sequences upload, deployment wait, run repeated by -runs (default one), then a single verify; run repetitions do not each perform verification.

Standalone run-pytest requires the first positional folder, checks direct test_*.py files and warns/returns if none exist, splits -pytest-args by whitespace before pytest.main and raises RuntimeError for nonzero pytest results; it does not upload or run first.

The -run-pytest folder option executes tests only after the selected non-run-pytest handler returns, including offline handlers; after test it follows upload/repeated runs/verify, while other main commands use the standalone warning about needing recent upload/run.

SesamParser errors exit 2, including explicit upload worker/rate validation, while unknown/missing commands, bootstrap failures, developer denial and command exceptions exit 1; dispatch catches BaseException including handler exits/interrupts, specially reports upload/testdata errors and limits generic underlying tracebacks to extra verbosity, while -version exits 0 before command admission.

Authentication dispatch uses manifest auth/variant to select Tripletex, OAuth2 with optional SuperOffice-ticket, or API-key login and sets service credentials from the resolved node; the API-key helper is invoked only when .authconfig exists, and unrecognized auth falls through without work.

OAuth2 authentication starts a Flask callback server on port 5010 and logs an authorization URL, exchanges callback codes against an external token endpoint, may call identity/SuperOffice services, writes secrets to all returned node systems and updates node environment; its shutdown helper shells out to lsof on port 5010 and kills the returned PIDs.

API-key login writes secrets to all returned systems and can exchange a manifest JWT login request for access/refresh tokens; unlike OAuth2/Tripletex, this inspected helper does not write environment variables despite its success message.

Tripletex login writes credentials to the selected placeholder system and updates environment/profile values, constructing a session token URL rather than directly requesting that token endpoint in this helper.

SuperOffice-ticket OAuth2 delegates to a helper that uses manifest JWKS and RSA_PRIVATE_KEY to obtain/verify external system-user ticket data and perform SuperOffice API requests, adding external boundaries beyond the basic OAuth2 token exchange.

Authentication helpers often catch errors and report failure through logs or callback text rather than raising to command dispatch, so successful CLI return does not reliably certify transactional secret/environment updates.

Credential logging is hazardous: SesamNode debug logging masks JWT but connection failure prints full URL/JWT, -vvv enables HTTP debugging, regular .jinja_vars values are logged, and --use-client-secret can place the client secret in the logged OAuth2 authorization URL; -skip-tls-verification affects the external node connection rather than establishing a universal policy for independent requests.

The connector modules provide expansion/collapse and login helpers rather than establishing the historical standalone connectorpy command dispatcher shown in README examples; connector_cli.__init__ is empty and sitecustomize adds connector directories to Python site paths.

The fair-weather shell scenario exercises credentialed reset, whitelisted test with post-command pytest, update, status, dump download and final reset, while its nested Python test only checks underscore-free pipe filenames/IDs; passing -sesamconfig-file there is not proof that the option has a consumer.

The embedded-conversion integration scenario copies local fixtures, wipes, converts, tests, resets and compares resulting trees; its before/after fixture specifically shows conditional test embedded source becoming http_endpoint while prod is unchanged.

test.sh performs executable help smoke checking and runs the authored scenario directories using a credentialed node, so these reset/wipe-containing checks are remote integration scenarios rather than safe offline contract tests.
